title: Keep speaker, source and authority distinct in shared event paths
summary: When adding new actor types to a shared message or event path, audit every attribution field instead of letting new speakers inherit assumptions designed for the original human-only path.

conditions: A system originally built around one human speaker adds agents, tools, services or other actor types.
Those actors use an existing shared message or event-writing path.
The existing path contains human-specific defaults for actor identity, provenance, authority or claim classification.
problem_pattern.failure_mode: A new actor can be recorded as though a human made the statement or decision. The ledger then preserves an event but misstates who acted, where the event came from, or what authority it carried.

generalised_method.action: List every actor type that can enter the shared write path, including humans, agents, tools, services and system processes.

Trace the path from the authenticated speaker identity to every persisted attribution field: actor, represented principal, recorder, provenance, authority, inference or claim kind, truth status and event type.
Derive each field from the evidence appropriate to that field. Do not reuse a human message default for an agent merely because both use the same message API.
Keep the performer distinct from any human or organisation represented by that performer. Record an on-behalf-of relationship only when there is explicit host evidence for it.
Do not treat participant type, membership or a role label as proof of identity authentication or decision authority. Use the host's authenticated identity and delegation evidence for those claims.

Test each actor type through the actual shared write path. Assert both the expected attribution and prohibited substitutions—for example, an agent event must not silently acquire human direct-user authority.
Retest established human paths and legacy compatibility after changing the shared mapping.

applicability: Multi-agent applications adding agents to an existing human-facing conversation or event API.
Event-sourced systems where several actor types share one append path.
Tool-using assistants where tool output, assistant reasoning and human decisions need different attribution.
Systems recording actions performed by an agent or service on behalf of another principal.
limitations: This method does not authenticate the speaker; the host must supply a trusted identity.
It does not define a permission model or prove that a represented principal authorised an action.
A participant type can guide expected handling but is not a substitute for evidence of provenance or authority.
Event labels and provenance values alone do not establish that a human saw, understood or approved an event.
This candidate comes from a real code-path correction in the AEL repository and its test suite, not from a production incident or an independently evaluated external team.

checks: The pre-change shared message path applied user provenance, direct-user authority and user-statement classification to every speaker.
The corrected path resolves the registered speaker and records human, agent, service, system and unknown speaker defaults separately.
The multi-agent fixture asserts distinct registered agent actor IDs, assistant provenance and no human direct-user authority for agent messages.
The fixture also asserts that human messages and human decisions remain separately attributed.
The AEL CI suite passed 88 tests on Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13 after the change.
not_established: Authentication behaviour of a live hosted chat or multi-agent platform.
Correctness of every possible host-specific provenance or delegation mapping.
A production incident rate or measured reduction in attribution errors.
Universal applicability without adapting the field mapping to the receiving system.

reuse_guidance: Use as an implementation review aid when adding actor types to a shared event path. Re-map the fields for the receiving system and verify trusted identity and authority evidence at the host boundary before relying on the resulting ledger.
